windows.notes:
Refract 1.5.6 for Windows fixes "Refract couldn't open Settings" (NullReferenceException).

The Settings window crashed while it was being built, before any page loaded, so every click on Settings ended in that message and the earlier retry hit the same crash. It now builds its navigation first, so Settings opens every time.

mac.notes:
Refract 1.5.7 for Mac gives the orb a new pattern every time it lights up, and keeps quick messages light.

The orb: each time you rewrite, the light inside the button picks one of six moods (Aurora, Tide, Swirl, Nebula, Spark or Drift), so it is never quite the same twice. The comet around the rim starts from a different spot each time too.

Quick messages: in an AI app, a very short note now only gets typo fixes and a short reply is only polished, instead of being rebuilt into a long prompt. A real task keeps the app's full preset. You can turn this off in Settings, General, Capture and paste. Review and adjust shows one version straight away, with one-tap Warmer, Firmer, More direct and More detail buttons. In Warp and in terminals, Refract rewrites only the highlighted text and copies the result, so it never selects your scrollback.

Also: model lists are tidier (OpenRouter shows its free models, OpenAI and ChatGPT show the newest ten), and the command-line tool and Undo stay responsive.

linux.notes:
Refract 1.5.7 for Linux brings the Mac's glowing orb to the prism and gives it a new pattern every time it lights up.

The orb: while a rewrite runs (and while you hold the prism down), soft light drifts and breathes inside the glass and a comet of light circles the rim, as on the Mac. Each time, it picks one of six moods (Aurora, Tide, Swirl, Nebula, Spark or Drift), so it is never quite the same twice. It is drawn straight to the screen now, so it stays smooth, and it holds still if you have animations turned off in GNOME.

Also: model lists are tidier (OpenRouter shows its free models, OpenAI and ChatGPT show the newest ten).
